qualifiers: one instrument, not a band or ensemble type

answers.name: Piano
answers.fact: Short for 'pianoforte': soft-loud, because it could play both.

answers.name: Guitar
answers.fact: Jimi Hendrix played right-handed guitars flipped upside down and restrung.

answers.name: Drums
answers.fact: The modern drum kit came together in New Orleans in the early 1900s.

answers.name: Violin
answers.fact: A Stradivarius sold for nearly US$16 million in 2011.

answers.name: Trumpet
answers.fact: Two trumpets were found in Tutankhamun's tomb.

answers.name: Flute
answers.fact: Flutes carved from bird bone go back around 40,000 years.

answers.name: Saxophone
answers.fact: Invented by Belgian Adolphe Sax in the 1840s.

answers.name: Bass guitar
answers.fact: Leo Fender's 1951 Precision Bass made the electric bass mainstream.

answers.name: Keyboard
answers.fact: A tiny Casio keyboard plays the riff on Trio's 1982 hit 'Da Da Da'.

answers.name: Theremin
answers.fact: Played without touching it: your hands move through its electric fields.

answers.name: Didgeridoo
answers.fact: Players circular-breathe to keep the drone going non-stop.

answers.name: Triangle
answers.fact: Liszt's first piano concerto gives it such a big part it got nicknamed the 'triangle concerto'.

answers.name: Cello
answers.fact: Yo-Yo Ma once left his US$2.5 million cello in a New York taxi. He got it back.

answers.name: Clarinet
answers.fact: 'Rhapsody in Blue' opens with a famous clarinet glissando.

answers.name: Harp
answers.fact: Ireland's national symbol, on its coins and passports.

answers.name: Trombone
answers.fact: Most use a slide, not valves, to change pitch.

answers.name: Tuba
answers.fact: The youngest orchestral brass instrument, patented in 1835.

answers.name: Ukulele
answers.fact: Brought to Hawaii by Portuguese immigrants. The name may mean 'jumping flea'.

answers.name: Harmonica
answers.fact: The first instrument played in space, on Gemini 6 in 1965.

answers.name: Accordion
answers.fact: Patented in Vienna in 1829.

answers.name: Bagpipes
answers.fact: Played across Europe and the Middle East, not just in Scotland.

answers.name: Banjo
answers.fact: Descends from instruments brought to the Americas by enslaved West Africans.

answers.name: Xylophone
answers.fact: Greek for 'wood sound'.

answers.name: Oboe
answers.fact: The whole orchestra tunes to its A.

answers.name: Bassoon
answers.fact: Over 2.5 metres of tube, folded in half.

answers.name: French horn
answers.fact: Unwound, its tubing would stretch about 3.7 metres.

answers.name: Double bass
answers.fact: The biggest and lowest of the orchestra's bowed strings.

answers.name: Viola
answers.fact: A little bigger than a violin, and tuned lower.

answers.name: Organ
answers.fact: The organ in Atlantic City's Boardwalk Hall has over 33,000 pipes.

answers.name: Synthesizer
answers.fact: Robert Moog's synths of the 1960s changed the sound of pop.

answers.name: Recorder
answers.fact: Henry VIII owned dozens of them.

answers.name: Tambourine
answers.fact: Frame drums with jingles go back thousands of years in the Middle East.

answers.name: Bongos
answers.fact: A pair of small Cuban hand drums.

answers.name: Mandolin
answers.fact: Tuned exactly like a violin.

answers.name: Glockenspiel
answers.fact: German for 'bell play'.

answers.name: Cymbals
answers.fact: Zildjian, the famous cymbal maker, was founded in Constantinople in 1623.

answers.name: Maracas
answers.fact: Traditionally dried gourds filled with seeds.

answers.name: Castanets
answers.fact: The clicking heartbeat of flamenco.

answers.name: Sitar
answers.fact: George Harrison brought it into Beatles songs after lessons with Ravi Shankar.

answers.name: Kazoo
answers.fact: You hum into it rather than blow.

answers.name: Piccolo
answers.fact: Half the size of a flute, and an octave higher.

answers.name: Timpani
answers.fact: Foot pedals let players retune them mid-piece.

answers.name: Snare drum
answers.fact: The rattle comes from wires stretched across the bottom skin.

answers.name: Cowbell
answers.fact: 'More cowbell' comes from a 2000 Saturday Night Live sketch.

answers.name: Steelpan
answers.fact: Invented in Trinidad and Tobago, hammered out of oil drums.

answers.name: Marimba
answers.fact: Wooden bars over resonator tubes, with roots in Africa and Central America.

answers.name: Harpsichord
answers.fact: Plucks its strings with quills rather than hitting them with hammers.

answers.name: Tabla
answers.fact: A pair of Indian hand drums that can bend their pitch.

answers.name: Djembe
answers.fact: A goblet-shaped West African drum played with bare hands.

answers.name: Lute
answers.fact: The Renaissance's go-to instrument.

answers.name: Lyre
answers.fact: Ancient Greek, and Apollo is usually shown holding one.

answers.name: Pan flute
answers.fact: Named after the Greek god Pan.

answers.name: Conga
answers.fact: Tall Afro-Cuban drums, usually played in twos or threes.

answers.name: Bugle
answers.fact: No valves: buglers change notes with their lips alone.

answers.name: Cornet
answers.fact: Like a trumpet, but more tightly coiled and mellower.

answers.name: Sousaphone
answers.fact: Designed for John Philip Sousa's band, to wrap around the player.

answers.name: Vibraphone
answers.fact: Spinning fans in its tubes create that shimmering vibrato.

answers.name: Ocarina
answers.fact: Made famous in games by The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time.

answers.name: Tin whistle
answers.fact: A six-hole whistle at the heart of Irish folk music.

answers.name: Vuvuzela
answers.fact: The droning soundtrack of the 2010 World Cup in South Africa.

answers.name: Euphonium
answers.fact: A small tuba-like horn, nicknamed 'the cello of the band'.

answers.name: Keytar
answers.fact: A keyboard you wear like a guitar.

answers.name: Bodhrán
answers.fact: An Irish frame drum played with a small double-ended stick.

answers.name: Shamisen
answers.fact: A three-stringed Japanese lute.

answers.name: Koto
answers.fact: Japan's national instrument: a long zither with 13 strings.

answers.name: Erhu
answers.fact: A two-stringed Chinese fiddle with the bow trapped between the strings.

answers.name: Pipa
answers.fact: A pear-shaped Chinese lute played for around 2,000 years.

answers.name: Guzheng
answers.fact: A Chinese zither with movable bridges under every string.

answers.name: Balalaika
answers.fact: A Russian folk lute with a triangular body.

answers.name: Bouzouki
answers.fact: The long-necked lute behind the Zorba the Greek theme.

answers.name: Handpan
answers.fact: The original, the Hang, was invented in Switzerland in 2000.

answers.name: Kalimba
answers.fact: A thumb piano with metal tines, from the African mbira family.

answers.name: Melodica
answers.fact: A little keyboard you blow into through a tube.

answers.name: Celesta
answers.fact: 'Dance of the Sugar Plum Fairy' made it famous.

answers.name: Hurdy-gurdy
answers.fact: A crank turns a rosined wheel that bows the strings.

answers.name: Zither
answers.fact: Its theme made the 1949 film The Third Man famous.

answers.name: Dulcimer
answers.fact: The hammered kind is struck with tiny mallets.

answers.name: Clavichord
answers.fact: So quiet it was mostly played at home.

answers.name: Harmonium
answers.fact: A pump organ that's now central to Indian and Pakistani music.

answers.name: Concertina
answers.fact: A small hexagonal squeezebox invented in England in 1829.

answers.name: Bandoneon
answers.fact: The heartbeat of Argentine tango, though it was invented in Germany.

answers.name: Musical saw
answers.fact: An ordinary handsaw, bent and bowed for an eerie wail.

answers.name: Jaw harp
answers.fact: One of the oldest instruments: twanged against your open mouth.

answers.name: Oud
answers.fact: A fretless Middle Eastern lute, ancestor of the European lute.

answers.name: Santoor
answers.fact: A hammered dulcimer from Kashmir.

answers.name: Shakuhachi
answers.fact: A Japanese bamboo flute once played by wandering Zen monks.

answers.name: Gamelan
answers.fact: Technically a whole Indonesian ensemble of gongs and metallophones.

answers.name: Cajón
answers.fact: A box drum you sit on, born in Peru.

answers.name: Washboard
answers.fact: A laundry board turned percussion by skiffle and zydeco bands.

answers.name: Flugelhorn
answers.fact: A wider, softer cousin of the trumpet.

answers.name: Contrabassoon
answers.fact: Its tubing runs to almost 6 metres.

answers.name: Cor anglais
answers.fact: Neither English nor a horn: it's an alto oboe.

answers.name: Bass clarinet
answers.fact: Curved like a saxophone at both ends, but it's a clarinet.

answers.name: Mellophone
answers.fact: Stands in for the French horn in marching bands.

answers.name: Steel guitar
answers.fact: The sound of country music's crying, sliding notes.

answers.name: Talking drum
answers.fact: A West African drum whose pitch can mimic the tones of speech.

answers.name: Spoons
answers.fact: A pair of spoons rattled against the knee in folk music.

answers.name: Sackbut
answers.fact: The Renaissance ancestor of the trombone.

answers.name: Crumhorn
answers.fact: A J-shaped Renaissance reed pipe with a buzzy tone.

answers.name: Serpent
answers.fact: A snake-shaped bass horn made of wood wrapped in leather.

answers.name: Ondes Martenot
answers.fact: An early electronic instrument Radiohead's Jonny Greenwood plays.

answers.name: Nyckelharpa
answers.fact: A Swedish keyed fiddle with extra strings that ring in sympathy.

answers.name: Duduk
answers.fact: An Armenian double-reed instrument made from apricot wood.

answers.name: Glass harmonica
answers.fact: Benjamin Franklin invented it in 1761: spinning glass bowls played with wet fingers.
